data.narrative:
D-Orbit, a Series C space and aerospace company that has raised $166M to date, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 5 public-market peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-sector participants including Sierra Space, Skyryse, and SpaceX.

Two valuation methods are applicable here. Stage-progression analysis, using a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implies a valuation of $282M from the $166M capital base. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $1.8B, with the peer set ranging from $1.15B (floor) to $8.0B (ceiling). The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in business model maturity and capital intensity within the space sector.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $240M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median outputs reflects tension between backward-looking capital efficiency metrics and forward-looking peer valuations in a capital-intensive, high-volatility sector. Public-market anchoring via P/S multiples (27.4x median across the comparable set) cannot be applied without D-Orbit's disclosed revenue. Key uncertainties include revenue scale, customer concentration, and the timing and capital requirements of next-stage milestones.
